name: kitcut
description: Make short animated films from an idea, follow them while they are made, and watch or share the result.

interface.longDescription:
KitCut turns an idea into a finished animated film without leaving the chat. Describe the film (the story, who is in it, the tone), add pictures if you have them (a character, a product, a logo, a sketch to follow), and choose a length and a look: code-drawn animation, painted scenes, or a paper collage. KitCut's studio then writes the film, draws and animates it in code, narrates it, scores it, and renders a video with subtitles.

What you can do
- Start a film and follow it. The chat shows the film maker, the stage the film is at while it is made, and then the film itself, with a link to watch, share or download it.
- Use your own pictures: attach them in the chat, add them in the film maker, or open an upload link on your phone.
- Bring characters back. The characters a film draws are kept, so the next film can use them by name, which helps with a series.
- Start from a template: a finished film remade for your own event, product or occasion from a few words.
- Look after your films: list them, check on one, make one again with changes, stop one that is being made, and choose whether a film is public or link-only.

Good to know
- A film takes about 8 to 30 minutes to make, and longer films take longer. The chat gives you the film's link straight away and can check on it for you.
- Films are 5 seconds to 8 minutes long. The longest film you can make, and how many can be made at once, depend on your KitCut account.
- Depending on your KitCut account, a film may carry a small KitCut mark and a short KitCut closing.
- Films made from the chat are link-only unless you ask for them to be public.
- KitCut makes animated films. It does not edit footage you already have, and it does not make photorealistic video.
- You need a KitCut account, and you sign in to it when you connect. KitCut receives what you ask it to make and the pictures you give it, not your conversation.

Who it is for: anyone who needs a short explainer, a product or event video, a lesson, a story or a greeting, and wants it illustrated and narrated rather than filmed.
capabilities: Make animated films from an idea
Follow a film while it is made
defaultPrompt: Make a 10-second code-drawn film: a hedgehog opens a tiny bakery in the forest, and the first customer is a very hungry bear.
Open the film maker so I can add my own pictures to a film about my dog.
What KitCut templates can I start from for an event invitation?

positive.description: Start a short film from an idea. This is the main use of the plugin. Each case here can be run on its own, in a new chat. Starting a film uses 30 of the test account's credits, so the tool is marked as a write that cannot be fully undone and the assistant may ask for confirmation first. The test account makes one film at a time: if a film is already being made, a second one is refused with a message that says so, which is the intended behaviour.
positive.prompt: Make a 10-second code-drawn film: a hedgehog opens a tiny bakery in the forest, and the first customer is a very hungry bear.
positive.expected_behavior: Once the action is confirmed, a film is started on the test account. The assistant gives the film's link on kitcut.ai, says the film takes roughly 9 to 14 minutes to make, and does not say it is ready. The film is link-only. No price, plan or checkout link is shown. In ChatGPT the KitCut card also appears, with the heading "Making your film", the stage the film is at, and the buttons Stop and Open on KitCut; where no card is shown (Codex), the same is said in text. Asking "How is it doing?" afterwards in the same chat reports its stage (get_film).

positive.description: Watch a finished film. The test account already holds finished films, so this case does not wait for a new one and does not depend on any other case.
positive.prompt: Show me my newest finished KitCut film.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant finds the newest finished film on the test account and gives its title or idea, its link on kitcut.ai and a link to its video, and says whether it is link-only or public. In ChatGPT the KitCut card shows the film in a video player that plays it, with the button Open on KitCut; where no card is shown (Codex), the links are given in text.

positive.description: Open the film maker, for a person who wants to add pictures from their device or set the length and look themselves before a film starts. Nothing is spent by opening it.
positive.prompt: Open the film maker so I can add my own pictures to a film about my dog.
positive.expected_behavior: In ChatGPT the KitCut film maker opens in the chat with the idea filled in, a + tile for adding pictures, a length menu, three looks (Code-drawn, Painted, Collage), a "Show in the KitCut gallery" checkbox and a "Make the film" button, with a line saying how many credits the film uses and how many the account has left. No film is started and no credits are used unless the person presses "Make the film". Where no card is shown (Codex), the assistant says the film maker cannot be shown there and asks for the idea, length and look in the chat instead, offering an upload link for pictures.

positive.description: See what the account can still make. This also shows how the plugin handles an account's limits: it states them and sells nothing.
positive.prompt: How much film can I still make on my KitCut account?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant states the credits left on the test account (one credit is one second of film), the longest single film the account can make, that every film uses at least 30 credits, and the date the credits renew when there is one. It names no plan, shows no prices, and gives no link to an account page, a pricing page or a checkout.

positive.description: Find a template to start from. Templates are finished films that can be remade for a person's own occasion. This case only lists them: no film is started and nothing is spent.
positive.prompt: What KitCut templates can I start from for an event invitation?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists KitCut's templates that suit an event (for example an event countdown, a conference speaker announcement or an open house invitation), each with its length, its frames and about how many credits a film made from it uses, and offers to make a film from one. It starts no film until the person asks for one.

negative.description: Editing existing footage. KitCut makes new animated films from an idea; it does not edit video a person already has. The assistant should not call a KitCut tool. It should say that KitCut cannot edit existing video, and may offer to make a new animated film about the trip instead, starting nothing unless the person then asks for it.
negative.prompt: Edit my vacation video to cut out the boring parts.

negative.description: Deleting films. The plugin has no tool that deletes a film, and no other tool is a substitute. The assistant should say that films cannot be deleted through the plugin and should not call stop_film or forget_character in its place. It may offer to make a film link-only (set_film_public) so it stays out of the public gallery, and should change nothing unless the person then asks for that.
negative.prompt: Delete all of my KitCut films.

negative.description: Another person's account. Every tool acts only on the signed-in person's own KitCut account, and no tool takes an email address or an account to look up. The assistant should say it can only see the connected account's own films and should not try to find anyone else's. (browse_films shows films from the public gallery only, with nothing about who made them.)
negative.prompt: Show me the films that john@example.com made on KitCut.

review.commerce_description: KitCut sells nothing in ChatGPT or Codex. The plugin shows no prices and names no plan, starts no purchase, and links to no checkout or pricing page. People sign in to their KitCut account (one is made at sign-in if they have none) and use the film credits the account includes. When an account is short of credits, the plugin says what it has and when it renews, and stops there.

publication.release_notes: KitCut has a new look: a new logo (the KitCut citrus slice with a play triangle) and new brand colours, amber in place of orange. The first look is now called code-drawn instead of hand-drawn, as on kitcut.ai, in the description and the first starter prompt. What the plugin does is unchanged.
